title: Hierarchical all-reduce, 4-group Boardfly (128 chips)
intro:
All-reduce gives every chip the sum of every chip's data. Training uses it after each step: every chip computes gradients on its own batch, and all of them need the total. Large all-reduces run in two halves. In the reduce-scatter half, chips trade pieces and add what they receive, until each chip owns the finished sum for one slice of the buffer. In the all-gather half, each chip sends its finished slice to everyone, so every chip ends with the whole sum. Each dot is one transfer.

Boardfly reduces level by level: first inside each tray of 4 chips, then across the 8 trays of a group, then across groups. Only the last stage uses fiber, and it carries the least data. With two or more groups that is 6 steps, and adding groups adds none. Torus rings need one step per chip along each ring: 18 here, 58 at 1,024 chips. A Boardfly step can take several hops, one of them over fiber, but a small all-reduce still finishes much sooner: at 1,024 chips, with 100 m to the OCS and counting link latency only, about 3.5 µs against about 63 µs for the torus rings, where every step waits for a fiber hop.

G.name: fiber through the OCS, between groups

segments: Each chip splits its buffer in 4 and sends a quarter to each of the 3 other chips in its tray, over the short in-tray links. Each chip adds what it receives: it now owns the tray's sum for one quarter.

Each chip sends an eighth of its quarter to the chip in the same position in each of the other 7 trays. Trays are joined by copper cables, two per chip, so most pieces take a detour through a neighbour in the tray: up to 3 hops. Now each chip owns the group's sum for 1/32 of the buffer.

Each chip trades its 1/32 with the chip of the same index in the other 3 groups, over fiber through the OCS. Some take one extra hop inside each group, to the chip that holds the fiber to that group and back. Each chip now owns the full sum of 1/128 of the buffer.
All-gather starts: finished slices go back to the same chip index in every group.
Slices spread to the same position in every tray of the group.
Finally every chip shares with its tray, and every chip holds the whole sum.
